svg.text: Rover Pi 3 B drives the Cytron MDDRC10 directly (no flight controller yet). Dashed parts are planned and not needed for the demo.
Each side's two motors in parallel. A side
runs backward: swap its two leads at the
MDDRC10. Lines crossing without a dot
PROBE mode: unplug the LEFT motor
pair from MLA/MLB, plug this in
Its own limit switches stop it at each end.
Bonnet uses SPI, CE1, GPIO22, GPIO25,
skips the Pi's input fuse: check
(Or power it by USB for the demo.)
cell: E+ E− A+ A− on the HX711
in probe holder v2, on the actuator
A/B swapped = no replies (not damage): swap them and retry.
Cable moves with the probe: leave a slack loop, anchor both ends.
PV in; BATTERY out → battery terminals
through its own fuse. Set battery type
1. Each ground symbol is its own wire to the fuse block's − bus; only the − bus wire goes to the battery −. Ring terminals on studs, ferrules in screw terminals.
2. E-stop: pressing it opens the relay coil loop, so the MDDRC10 loses motor power. The Pi, radio and sensor stay on (F3, F4) to report the stop.
3. Relay harnesses often have a coil diode: 86 = +, 85 = ground. Check the listing's diagram.
4. First power-up: wheels off the ground, E-stop pressed, start rover.py (it sends 'stop' pulses), then switch on. The MDDRC10 learns 'stop' at power-up.
5. MIX mode for the demo (the code mixes throttle and steering). The FDR's rev A drawing used INDEPENDENT mode with the Arduino; this one replaces it.
6. Check with i2cdetect -y 1: 3c (OLED) and 68 (MPU-6050). Turn on I2C in raspi-config.
7. Battery: charge LiFePO4 at 14.4 V; unplug the XT60 to charge on the bench.
D.I.R.T.T. rover wiring, demo configuration. Generated by code/Demo/wiring/make_rover_wiring.py. Fuse and wire sizes from the FDR drivetrain wiring (rev A).
